text: It is better, therefore, to conquer it than to cheat it; for a grief which has been deceived and driven away either by pleasure or by business rises again, and its period of rest does but give it strength for a more terrible attack; but a grief which has been conquered by reason is appeased for ever.
author: Lucius Annaeus Seneca
locator: Of Consolation, to his Mother Helvia, Chapter 17
